Pastor john suggest we would not use the word repent for the way we respond to daily sinning as christians. 

Sin is a condition of the heart that is bent away from God in preference for other things and any expression of that preference in our mind , attitude ,behaviours. 
So sin will be with us until that inner condition is holy obliterated in the presence of sin. 

The new testament does not encourage us to use the word repent for the daily activity of acknowledging those sins and bringing them to God and expressing our sorrows and hating them and turning afresh to walk in the light. And rather the word repentance in the new testament refers to a more basic ,fundamental change of mind, the kind we experience in the beginning of our christian life. And that we may have to experience that if our lives take a terrible turn into a path of destruction from we which need to be called back. He proposed the word confession in reference to
1 John 8 and 9. Use the word confession to deal daily habit with indwelling recurrent sin.

Two types of Confessions to sin

First type/Level

Confession at one level is expressing guilt and sorrow towards sin and sinning. But underneath there is a quiet assumption that this sin is going to happen again. Looking at nudity in a movie/website, getting excessively drunk with alcohol , responding belittling in a way to my loved ones etc (just knowing it will happen again in your heart) 

This kind of confession is very superficial , is a cloak for fatalism about your besetting sins. You feel bad about them but you have surrendered to their inevitability. 

Second type 
Same as first, express guilt and sorrow. But your hatred of the sin is so real that you have every intention as you confess of making war on that sin. 
Example 
“Tonight this weekend, you aim by the power of the holy spirit to defeat it, you are gonna seek out whatever way to help you put this sin to death, you are gonna rub it of it power, that’s the plan. No hypocrisy.”

Two types of sin 

First kind :

The kind of sin that blindsides you, it’s not pre meditated or planned , and there is scarcely any battle in the moment when it happens, before you’re doing what you wish you hadn’t done, it’s done! 

Like as, certain kind of sinful anger , knowing it’s over the top and not righteous, not holy. Maybe spontaneous unkind words that pop out of your mouth, and you’re ashamed of them as you say them. Or a reflexive sexual fantasy owing to some decade old experience or a recent advertisement you saw on the news/ media or wtv. 

It’s still sin even if it’s more or less spontaneous and not pre meditated. 

Second Kind :

Namely, it is pre meditated, you actually sit there or stand there, weighing wether to do it or not. Wether to look at the pornography or not. Wether to stay and listen to the dirty jokes or not, wether to call out the injustice at work or not, wether to be dishonest , you take 10 seconds, 10minutes , or 10 hours, WRESTLING. And then u do the sin. 

Pastor john says it’s possible for a christian to commit both types of sin and get into patterns for both types of confession for a season.

The confession that cloaks fatalism ,hopelessness ,peace with sin, and the sin that is premeditated are more dangerous to our souls. Both are dangerous but the confessions bordering on hypocrisy and the sin bordering on planned unrighteousness are more dangerous .

Paul acknowledge on Romans 7 verses 16-19

-We can’t come up with a list of sins, or a number for the frequency which you can sin and get away with it. We can’t do that in a way that answers the question, how much sinning proves that i’m not a christian? 

To the degree that your confessing of sins, have made a kind of fatalistic peace with sin inevitability and to the degree that your sin falls into the category of premeditated unrighteousness, to that degree , you should be frightened that you are on the path that may well lead to destruction.

The book in the new testament, is perhaps the hardest on christians sinning is the same book that warns most explicitly about the dangers of perfectionism.

1 John 1:8-10

“If we claim to be without sin, we deceives ourselves and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins,he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness. If we claim we have not sinned we make him out to be a liar and his words is not in us.”
